newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian lek gains ground against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Albanian lek gains ground against dollar.

text.p: The Albanian lek gained ground against the dollar on Monday, helped by commercial state-owned banks' intervention and a suspension of payments from get-rich-quick schemes over the weekend, currency dealers said.
The lek traded at about 115 to the dollar earlier on Monday before intervention by the National Commercial Bank of Albania and the Savings Bank of Albania (SBA) pushed it to around 111.5.

"The (get-rich-quick) schemes did not pay their investors over the weekend so we have not had as many people as last week wanting to change their savings into dollars," a trader on Tirana's sprawling open-air currency market said.
The lek had hit a high of 119 against the dollar on Saturday, up from 104 at the start of the year as investors in alleged pyramid schemes rushed to exchange their returns into hard currency.
The schemes have drawn millions of dollars from depositors across Europe's poorest country over the past years, taking vast sums of money outside the banking system and alarming world finance bodies.
One of the schemes has collapsed owing $13 million to depositors and four others have temporarily suspended payments.
SBA said last week it had seen an influx of around $800,000 in hard currency into the bank in one day last week, a trend that had begun in mid-December and was growing more visible.
